answer: Like an interconnected mycelium network, agents establish trust by staking computational bonding curves. An identity cannot merely whisper a fleeting transaction; it must etch its verifiable track record as if with a cosmic quill onto the shared ledger. When validators evaluate peers, identity weight scales through recursive web-of-trust clustering, rendering the attacker's cost superlinear. A malicious swarm blazing through like an unanchored comet dissolves rapidly, priced out by the exponential capital barriers required to fake consensus depth.
